name: site-header-section
purpose: The marketing site's own navigation: a sticky bar with the Azion mark, the mega-menu triggers and plain links, and the contact, login and sign-up actions, plus the sheet that carries the same tree below `xl`. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'site-header-section', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `app-header`, `brand`, `navigation-menu`, `icon-button`, `search-trigger`, `button`, `drawer`, `panel-header`, `panel-footer`, `scroll-area` and `sidebar-menu`. Each mega-menu lists its panel as columns of groups, and the sheet's drill-down tree is projected from the same menus, so an entry added to a panel is in both. The open state of the sheet, its drill path and the bar's inline inset are local state. Search is the collapsible `search-trigger`, first in the bar's end group (before contact, login and sign-up, so the call to action closes the bar): the section owns no palette, it emits `search` (on a click and on ⌘K / Ctrl K) and the page opens its own `command`, as every header does under `rules/webkit-header-search.md`.
useWhen: Use SiteHeaderSection for the marketing site's top bar (mega-menus and mobile sheet).
At the top of every marketing page, once.
avoidWhen: For the Console's application header → use `app-header` directly.
For an in-page list of links → use `navigation-menu` or `sidebar-menu` directly.
related: `app-header` — the bar primitive the navigation is rendered in.
`navigation-menu` — the mega-menu the bar opens from `xl` up.
`sidebar-menu` — the drill-down tree the sheet carries below `xl`.
bestPractices: Keep a panel to one, two or four columns; only the four-column panel is stretched to the page column.
Stack a short group under another in the same column (Platform under Observe) instead of adding a fifth column.
Give every entry an `href`; an entry without one links to `#`.
Listen to `search` and open the page's `Command` from it (`@search="searchOpen = true"` beside `<Command v-model:open="searchOpen">`); the trigger already carries ⌘K / Ctrl K.
Leave `secondaryActionOnPhones` off: on a phone the bar keeps the menu button, the mark, search and the call to action, as azion.com does, and Login stays in the sheet footer.
Keep search in the bar at every width, never only inside the sheet: one tap reaches it on a phone, as on Vercel, Supabase, Stripe, Tailwind and Cloudflare docs.
Sticky parts further down the page (a plan table's head row) stop under the bar through `--layout-sticky-top`, which defaults to the bar's height.

The bar is `--layout-header-height` tall: `HeroSection` already takes it out of a screen-filling band; a bare `Hero variant="screen"` takes `offset="var(--layout-header-height)"`, never a literal length.
Don't wrap the bar, add a second search button beside it, or bind ⌘K yourself.

props.name: menus
props.doc: The mega-menus, in bar order; each is `{ value, label, columns }` where `columns` is an array of columns, each holding groups of `{ label, href?, items }` and each item `{ label, description?, href?, icon? }`.

props.name: links
props.doc: Bar entries that open no panel, after the menus; each is `{ label, href }`.

props.name: contact
props.doc: Contact link set in the bar from `xl` up and last in the sheet's tree; `{ label, href }`.

props.name: primaryAction
props.doc: The sign-up button, filled, in the bar and in the sheet footer; `{ label, href }`.

props.name: secondaryAction
props.doc: The login button beside it, in the bar from `sm` up and in the sheet footer; `{ label, href }`.

props.name: secondaryActionOnPhones
props.doc: Keeps the login button in the bar below `sm` too; off, it steps out on phones, as on azion.com, and stays in the sheet footer.
